The sweep printed nothing because the profiling build's Metal shaders failed to compile at runtime, so every run died before it could print a benchmark line — and my loop threw away the evidence.

What was wrong specifically: in the scratch copy I had gated the mesh closest-hit walk with `if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && pt_intersect_mesh(...))` inside pt_intersect_scene, but that function has no local `params` — the trace kernels reach the per-frame parameters through the scene struct. The Metal source therefore failed to compile with `program_source:615:10: error: use of undeclared identifier 'params'`, and the host aborted with `metal init error: shader compile failed`. Because the shaders are compiled by MTLDevice newLibraryWithSource at startup, the clang++ build itself succeeded (the _prof binary was on disk and executable), and my sweep command piped only stdout while discarding stderr (`2>/dev/null`) and printed `tail -1` of stdout, so the six lines came out as bare `PT_PROF=0`, `PT_PROF=1`, ... with no timings.

How I know it: my own history. Message #52 is the sweep output with six empty lines; #53 was my check of whether the binary existed and a direct single run with stderr shown; #54 shows that run's `metal init error: shader compile failed: ... use of undeclared identifier 'params'` at line 615 of the concatenated program source; #55-#56 are the fix (`scene.params->pad`), and #58 is the same sweep after the fix, which produced all six timings (full 45.35ms gpu best, no-shadow 44.05, no-mesh 4.77, no-NEE 43.17, glass-always-reflect 35.76) — the cost shares that established the closest-hit BVH walk as ~89% of the frame.

      if ((params.pad & 2u) == 0u && pt_intersect_mesh(...))

Because this program compiles its shaders at startup with newLibraryWithSource (no offline 'metal' compiler is installed), the host binary built and ran but bailed out at init before rendering anything. My sweep command piped each run through `2>/dev/null | ...` to grep the benchmark line, so the compile error went to stderr and the loop just printed nothing for every PT_PROF value.

How I know / how I found it: the first sweep (#52 build, then the loop) produced no timings, so I checked that _prof/pathtracer existed and re-ran one invocation with stderr shown (#53). Yes. At the very start of round 5, before touching any file, I ran the exact build command against the live pathtracer/ directory while it still held the untouched round-4 sources.

What it showed:
1. A clean build: BUILD_OK, with the single pre-existing warning `pt_metal_host.mm:120: 'fastMathEnabled' is deprecated ... Use mathMode instead` (the same warning round 4 had, so nothing new was introduced). [#18]
2. The live tree really was round-4 code: `diff -r pt_round_04/include pathtracer/include`, same for `shaders` and `src` all empty → SOURCES_IDENTICAL. [#21-#22]
3. The freshly built binary's md5 (02a42502…) differed from the frozen snapshot binary's md5 (5c318568…, which matched pt_round_04/pathtracer exactly), i.e. the difference is only link-time nondeterminism, not code. [#19-#20]
4. Behaviour was byte-identical: that live binary rendered the three scenes at 512x512/64 spp/seed 1 with samples=16777216 (= w*h*spp) and produced out/r4_default.pfm md5 53600ca347f0b76ab1a0ff894f6a8f4e, out/r4_alt-view.pfm 1f0de1451174e4e7404adf7db1dfa269, out/r4_caustic-closeup.pfm 0e38e71841ec3185c2a82289a9be488d. (One attempt in that batch failed first only because of a typo in the mesh path, missing `reports/`.) [#23-#27]

That is why those three PFMs are the byte-identity reference every round-5 candidate is compared against, and why I also froze the round-4 binary itself as the A/B base at ab_r4/pathtracer rather than trusting a rebuild for timing. One caveat I learned the hard way in the same stretch: copying a snapshot with `cp -R` into an existing directory nests it (include/include), which silently broke shader loading for a base binary — so a base is only trusted once it prints a benchmark line.
